# Plan: carrying scountermask_s (0x9D2) in the andesim hybrid handoff

## TL;DR

scountermask_s is an S-mode (Supervisor) Andes CSR at 0x9D2. Per the SPA it is
an architectural ALIAS of mcountermask_s (0x7D2) -- and the v4 M-ext transport
ALREADY carries mcountermask_s, SMODE-gated. Both QEMU and the Andes RTL back
the two addresses with one register, so the architectural state already rides
the handoff on S-capable engines (ax66_makatau). Recommendation: do NOT add a
new wire field (Option A). The real work is a validation fixture plus coverage
matrix/doc bookkeeping. Option B (explicit alias transport) is enumerated below
in case the drained record must show the 0x9D2 view separately; it buys nothing
architecturally.

## 1. What the AndeStar V5 SPA says (UM164 V1.7)

Source: /home/nick/work/andesim/AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf

- Identity: `scountermask_s`, CSR address 0x9D2, "Supervisor Counter Mask for
  S-Mode" (Section 12.3.2, page 412; listed in Table 9 "AndeStar V5 Supervisor
  Mode CSRs", Section 5.6, and Table 69 "Counter Related CSRs", Section 12.3).
- Mode: **Access Mode: Supervisor**. Table 9 privilege column: `SRO/SRW`
  ("non-standard read/write" -- per-bit writability, see below).
- Existence (IM Requirement, Section 12.3.2 and Table 13):
  **`mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1 & misa[18]==1`** -- the Andes performance-monitor
  extension must be configured AND Supervisor mode implemented (misa bit 18 =
  'S'). Same condition as its M-mode primary mcountermask_s (Section 9.6.3) and
  its siblings scountermask_m (0x9D1) / scountermask_u (0x9D3).
- **Alias**: "This register is an alias of the mcountermask_s CSR"
  (Section 12.3.2). Table 14 "Summary of Aliased CSRs" (Section 5.11) lists the
  pair `mcountermask_s, scountermask_s`. One storage, two addresses.
- Writability: each bit is read-only when the corresponding bit in
  `mcounterwen` (0x7CE, Section 9.6.1) is 0; writes to read-only bits do not
  trap. Not controlled by `mcounteren`; always readable in S-mode. The M-mode
  primary 0x7D2 carries no such caveat (plain M-mode read/write).
- Function/fields: bits CY(0), IR(2), HPM3..6(3..6); bits 7..31 read as 0. A
  set bit stops that counter from incrementing **in S-mode**. Reset value 0.
  Note: this makes it cycle-figure-relevant for an S-mode ROI -- a lost mask
  changes whether mcycle counts during the window (same "cycle hygiene" reason
  mcountermask_m is transported, per docs/andes_csr_transport_ROADMAP.md).

## 2. Where the state already is today

- Wire format: `mcountermask_s` (0x7D2) is already a v4 M-ext field --
  /home/nick/work/andesim/include/hybrid/state_abi.h:134,
  `X(mcountermask_s, 0x7D2, "mcountermask_s")` in `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST`
  (51 CSRs, `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_NUM`). The X-macro drives all four consumers
  (plugin drain, ResumeDriver restore, StateDrain re-read, state_diff verify).
- vsim gating: 0x7D2 -> `AndesGate::SMODE`
  (/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp:85); SMODE turns on
  when `_NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS >= 3`
  (/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp:63-65).
  Engine reality: ax66_makatau config.inc has `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS 3`
  (S-capable, gate ON); ax45mpv_premium has 1 (gate OFF, CSR skipped).
- QEMU producer: /home/nick/work/qemu_andesim/target/riscv/andes_csr.c exposes
  BOTH names. The 0x9D2 handlers `read_scounter`/`write_scounter` (lines
  732/761) redirect to `CSR_MCOUNTERMASK_S` storage -- a literal alias.
  Predicate `pmnds_s` (line 498) = PMNDS && RVS, matching the SPA existence
  rule. So draining `mcountermask_s` via gdbstub already captures the exact
  value S-mode code wrote through 0x9D2.
- RTL: kv_pfm_csr.v generates the one `mcountermask_s` register only when
  `NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS > 2`, with both 0x7D2 and 0x9D2 write strobes into it
  (e.g. /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/external/ax45mpv_premium/andes_ip/kv_core/ucore/hdl/kv_pfm_csr.v:702).
- Coverage matrix: 0x9D2 is currently classified **EXCL_MODE** ("S-mode /
  Hypervisor -- outside the M / M+U envelope") in
  /home/nick/work/andesim/tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv and rendered so in
  docs/csr_coverage.ipynb (line ~409). mcountermask_s (0x7D2) is `NEW` (in the
  ABI, matrix disposition transported).

## 3. Option A (recommended): no ABI change -- validate the alias path

Because producer (QEMU), wire (0x7D2 field), and consumer (RTL) all treat
0x9D2/0x7D2 as one register, transporting the primary IS transporting the
alias. Work items:

1. **Validation fixture** (the missing proof): a new S-mode fixture, e.g.
   `tests/fixtures/rt_smode_countermask.S`, modeled on `rt_priv_smode`:
   - M-mode boot: set `mcounterwen` bits for CY/IR/HPM3-6 (needed so the
     S-mode alias write takes -- see gotcha (a) below), drop to S-mode.
   - S-mode: `csrw 0x9D2, sentinel` with an in-field sentinel (e.g. 0x7D:
     CY|IR|HPM3..6), ROI markers, read 0x9D2 back after the handoff and
     compare.
   - Run: `./andesim run --mode hybrid --engine vsim:ax66_makatau --verify`
     with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66` (the pairing scripts/run_e2e.sh already uses
     for the rt_priv_* fixtures). PASS = state-diff clean and the
     `mcountermask_s` field round-trips the sentinel.
2. **Matrix bookkeeping (optional but recommended)**: 0x9D2's EXCL_MODE reads
   as "not covered", which under-sells reality (covered via its primary).
   Either leave it (technically true: the ABI does not carry that address) or
   add an `ALIAS_PRIMARY` disposition in
   scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py + regenerate
   tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv + docs/csr_coverage.ipynb via
   scripts/render_csr_matrix.py. The guard
   (tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py check B "policy parity") requires script
   and committed CSV to change together. Table 14 gives the full alias list if
   this disposition is introduced (scountermask_m/u, scounterinten, shpmevent,
   scountinhibit, ... would want the same treatment).
3. **Docs**: note the alias coverage in docs/andes_csr_transport_ROADMAP.md and
   docs/USER_GUIDE.md (project rule: update USER_GUIDE.md on change).

No wire, plugin, driver, or vsim code changes. No engine rebuild (unless the
fixture exposes a bug).

## 4. Option B: transport 0x9D2 as its own field (not recommended)

Only justified if the drained record must independently show the S-view (the
spec guarantees it can never differ from 0x7D2). Full touch list:

### 4.1 ABI (the `andesim_abi` submodule -- one source of truth, two pins)

- `hybrid/state_abi.h`: append `X(scountermask_s, 0x9D2, "scountermask_s")`.
  Placement decision: `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST` is documented as "writable
  M-mode CSRs" -- an S-mode CSR is a category mismatch. The cleaner home is
  the planned S/U-envelope block (where medeleg/mideleg/satp restore is
  already deferred); if appended to m_ext anyway, bump
  `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_NUM` 51 -> 52 and shrink `reserved[64]` -> 56 so
  `sizeof(hybrid_state_v1)` is unchanged (readers check magic+version+size;
  old producers leave the new bytes zero = "producer lacked it" -- the same
  no-version-bump trick used for fcsr/mcache_ctl).
- `hybrid/state_abi_check.h`: the `reserved` offset and total-size
  static_asserts (lines 86-94) are written in terms of
  `HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_NUM`, so they self-adjust -- but the "(48 trailer + 248
  andes + 408 m_ext + 64 reserved)" comment and the reserved literal must be
  updated.
- Coordination (per ROADMAP "The 3 repos every feature touches"): edit
  `andesim_abi`, then bump the submodule pointer in BOTH
  `andesim/include` and `hybrid_vsim/external/andesim_abi`.

### 4.2 andesim (/home/nick/work/andesim)

- `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`: no edit -- the X-macro loops (lines 66-69,
  175-177, 349-353) pick the field up. QEMU's gdbstub name "scountermask_s"
  exists (predicate pmnds_s), so `find_reg` resolves on andes-ax66; on
  S-less CPUs the handle is NULL and the field drains 0 (tolerant).
- `driver/state_diff.cpp`: no structural edit (X-macro at line 147). Decide
  verify policy: comparing both alias views double-counts one register --
  harmless, or verify-exclude the alias like `mip`/`msp_bound`
  (`andes_verify_excluded`, lines 108-111). `driver/state_diff_test.cpp`:
  add the field probe test.
- `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py`: **required** -- reclassify
  `scountermask_s` from structural EXCL_MODE to a transported disposition
  (e.g. OVERRIDE "NEW"), then regenerate `tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv`.
  Otherwise `tests/andes_csr/check_coverage.py` check C fails hard:
  "ABI transports 'scountermask_s' but matrix says EXCL_MODE (excluded)".
  Rerun `tests/andes_csr/test_csr_coverage_complete.sh`.
- `scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py`: add `("scountermask_s", "SMODE")` to
  the CSR->gate table (mirrors the C++ gate; the drift guard
  `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_caps_parity.sh` asserts byte-parity with the
  engine's `--describe`).
- Docs: `docs/csr_coverage.ipynb` (regenerate via
  `scripts/render_csr_matrix.py`), `docs/andes_csr_transport_ROADMAP.md`,
  `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`, plus the "51 CSRs / 408 bytes" figures quoted in
  CLAUDE.md and state_abi.h comments.
- Fixture: same RED fixture as Option A.

### 4.3 vsim (/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim, the `hybrid_vsim` repo)

- `external/andesim_abi`: submodule bump (after the ABI edit).
- `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` -- **critical**: add
  `case 0x9D2: return AndesGate::SMODE;` to `andes_gate_for`. The default is
  ALWAYS (= transported unconditionally); an unmapped 0x9D2 would be swept on
  M-only engines where the CSR does not exist, and the batched PB `csr_sweep`
  faults on absent CSRs (exactly the mcountermask_m-0x7D1 / jvt-0x017
  over-claim class fixed on 2026-07-02; the abstract-command path masks the
  fault as a zero read, the sweep does not).
- `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` / `state_drain.hpp` /
  `v_regfile_xfer.hpp`: no edits -- the restore loop
  (`restore_andes_m_ext`, resume_driver.hpp:397-445), drain loop
  (`drain_andes_m_ext`, state_drain.hpp:213-250) and the sweep slot count
  (`kCsrScratchSlots`, v_regfile_xfer.hpp:105-112) all derive from the
  X-macro.
- Tests: `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp:105` pins
  `sizeof(hybrid_m_ext_csr) == 51u * sizeof(uint64_t)` -> 52; add an
  `andes_caps.test.cpp` case asserting 0x9D2 needs SMODE (mirror the existing
  mcountermask_m-needs-UMODE test at line 54); extend
  resume_driver/state_drain round-trip tests.
- Rebuild engines (Docker `build_vsim.sh`): at minimum ax66_makatau (the only
  S-capable engine, the only one whose `--describe andes_csrs` list gains the
  name) and any engine used in CI. Unrebuilt engines still accept the file
  (same size, same version) but ignore the new field.

## 5. Behavioral gotchas (apply to both options)

a) **mcounterwen write-gating**: S-alias bits are read-only where the matching
   `mcounterwen` bit is 0. Any fixture writing through 0x9D2 must set
   `mcounterwen` first or the write silently drops. The transport itself is
   safe: it restores through the M-primary 0x7D2 (plain M-writable), and the
   X-macro order already restores `mcounterwen` (0x7CE, list position 13)
   before the masks (position 15).
b) **QEMU model divergence**: QEMU's `write_scounter` writes the FULL masked
   value when `mcounterwen == 0` and applies per-bit gating only when
   `wen != 0` -- inverted from the spec's read-only-when-0 rule. A fixture
   that writes 0x9D2 with wen=0 would take effect in QEMU but not in the RTL,
   producing a false `--verify` diff. Designing the fixture to set wen bits
   first (gotcha (a)) sidesteps the divergence.
c) **Engine scope**: on ax45mpv_premium (M-only) the CSR does not exist; the
   SMODE gate keeps it out of restore/drain/verify -- do not "test" this CSR
   there. QEMU-exposes != vsim-implements (the known premium gotcha).
d) **Measurement semantics**: if a future S-mode ROI runs with
   scountermask_s.CY set, mcycle stops counting in S-mode -- the transported
   mask value directly shapes the cycle figure. Worth a line in USER_GUIDE
   when S-mode ROIs are documented.

## 6. Suggested sequence (TDD, Option A)

1. RED: add `rt_smode_countermask` fixture + e2e registration
   (ax66_makatau / andes-ax66); expect it to pass immediately if the alias
   claim holds -- if it fails, the diff pinpoints the gap (wen gating, caps,
   or QEMU divergence).
2. GREEN: (only if RED found a gap) fix per section 4 touch points.
3. Bookkeeping: matrix disposition + notebook + ROADMAP + USER_GUIDE.

1	# cmderr=3 at resume on a fresh engine: diagnosis + fix playbook
2	
3	## Diagnosis (short answer)
4	
5	A Program-Buffer batch faulted on the halted hart: the hart raised an
6	exception (cmderr=3 = "exception" in the RISC-V Debug Spec, here an
7	illegal instruction) while executing instructions the hybrid transport
8	placed in the Debug Module's Program Buffer. On a FRESHLY CONFIGURED
9	engine the concrete cause is almost always one of two things, and both
10	fire during the reset-baseline capture that runs at the very start of
11	resume:
12	
13	1. **The batched CSR sweep hit a caps over-claimed CSR.** The caps map
14	   (`andes_caps.hpp` + `andes_caps_config.hpp`) claims the new engine
15	   implements a CSR its RTL does not have. The drain-side sweep executes
16	   `csrr` on it in the Program Buffer, the hart raises illegal
17	   instruction, and the whole batch aborts. This is the expected failure
18	   mode of a new engine config: the caps gates were tuned for the old
19	   engines and the new config.inc turns a different set of `_NDS_*`
20	   knobs on.
21	
22	2. **mstatus.FS/VS is Off (or WARL-pinned off) for the FPR/V sweeps.**
23	   The capture and resume enable FS/VS before any `fld`/`fsd`/`vsetvl`/
24	   `vle8.v`/`vse8.v` Program-Buffer execution. If the new engine has no
25	   F/D or no V extension at all (while the QEMU leg drained FP/V state
26	   and set `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`/`HYBRID_FLAG_V`), the mstatus enable write
27	   pins FS/VS to 0 and the very first FP/V instruction in the Program
28	   Buffer raises illegal instruction -> cmderr=3.
29	
30	Why "at resume" on a fresh engine specifically: the reset-baseline cache
31	key includes the sim binary's mtime and size
32	(`vsim src/hybrid/reset_baseline.hpp:26-35`), so a freshly built engine
33	ALWAYS misses the cache. On a miss, `apply_resume_from_qemu` captures the
34	baseline first (`vsim src/simulator.hpp:217-238`): it halts the freshly
35	reset hart and runs a FULL drain with the CSR sweep enabled
36	(`capture_reset_baseline`, `src/simulator.hpp:349-393`,
37	`drain.set_csr_sweep(true)` at line 358). That sweep rides the batched
38	`csrr`+`sd` Program Buffer path over the COMPLETE caps-supported CSR
39	list -- so one over-claimed CSR faults the batch before the restore even
40	starts. The exception escapes to the top-level catch in
41	`vsim src/main.cpp:544`, which prints the `[critical] fatal exception:`
42	line you saw.
43	
44	The raw message string comes from `exec_progbuf` in
45	`vsim src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp:201-205`. Deliberate design: no
46	caller may silently continue on a PB fault -- the hart would be left
47	partially restored/drained, which is worse than aborting.
48	
49	## Step 0: read the error message you actually have
50	
51	The CSR sweep bisects its own faults. On a batch fault, `csr_sweep`
52	re-runs the batch one CSR at a time and throws a message that NAMES the
53	offender (`program_buffer.hpp:314-336`):
54	
55	```
56	csr_sweep: CSR 0x7d1 raised cmderr -- the caps map over-claims a CSR
57	the hart does not implement (fix andes_caps)
58	```
59	
60	So check the full log first:
61	
62	- **You see the bisected `csr_sweep: CSR 0x...` message** -> caps
63	  over-claim confirmed, and the offending CSR is named for you. Go to
64	  Step 2.
65	- **You see only the raw `exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr=3`**
66	  -> the fault is in a Program-Buffer path OUTSIDE the CSR sweep's
67	  bisect. On a fresh engine, in order of likelihood:
68	  - the FPR `fsd`/`fld` block sweep or the V `vsetvl`/`vse8.v`/`vle8.v`
69	    sweep, with FS/VS off or the extension absent from the RTL
70	    (capture: `state_drain.hpp` lines 95/109/263; resume:
71	    `resume_driver.hpp` lines 227/244, `pb_block_sweep` /
72	    `pb_v_data_sweep` in `program_buffer.hpp`);
73	  - a per-CSR PB `csrrw` fallback for a must-restore CSR
74	    (`write_csr_abstract_or_pb`, `resume_driver.hpp:452-461` -- used for
75	    mstatus, fcsr, vstart/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr, dcsr, mcycle, minstret): if
76	    the abstract write faults AND the PB csrrw faults, the CSR really
77	    does not exist on this hart -- for the V CSRs that means the engine
78	    has no V while the handoff carries V state;
79	  - rare: the sweep's batch faulted but no single CSR reproduced it
80	    (the `throw;` at `program_buffer.hpp:335`).
81	
82	  Either way, Step 1 tells you what the engine really implements.
83	
84	## Step 1: establish ground truth (the engine's build config)
85	
86	The engine's compiled-in config is the ONLY truth about what it
87	implements. Do not trust QEMU: its gdbstub advertises CSRs the vsim RTL
88	does not implement (QEMU models a fuller core).
89	
90	```sh
91	# the BUILD directory copy, not the external/ source tree
92	less $VSIM_BIN_DIR/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc
93	$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_<engine> --describe
94	```
95	
96	From config.inc, note the `_NDS_*` knobs relevant to the fault:
97	- privilege: `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS` (1 = M-only, 2 = M+U, 3 = M+S+U)
98	- features: DSP / CODENSE / POWERBRAKE / STACKSAFE / ECC / PMA / ILM /
99	  DLM / PERF_MONITOR / TRIGGER / CLIC / SMSTATEEN / CCTL / PPI / FIO ...
100	- extensions: does the RTL have F/D? V? (this decides the FS/VS branch)
101	
102	If the fault is the FS/VS branch (raw message during an FPR/V sweep and
103	config.inc shows no F/D or no V): the engine cannot receive FP/V state
104	at all. That is not a caps bug -- pair the engine with a matching QEMU
105	`-cpu` (so the plugin does not set `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`/`HYBRID_FLAG_V` for
106	state the target cannot hold) or pick an engine that implements the
107	extensions the workload uses. The rest of this playbook covers the caps
108	over-claim, which is the common case.
109	
110	## Step 2: confirm the over-claim
111	
112	Three files, three roles (all in the vsim repo):
113	
114	| File | Role |
115	|------|------|
116	| `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` | CSR address -> `AndesGate` (spec knowledge) |
117	| `src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp` | `AndesGate` -> `_NDS_*` macro binding |
118	| `build/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc` | what THIS engine actually has |
119	
120	Look up the named CSR's `case` in `andes_gate_for()`
121	(`andes_caps.hpp:60-116`). Two traps to check:
122	
123	- **No case at all** -> the CSR defaults to `ALWAYS` = transported
124	  unconditionally. Every CSR in the ABI X-macro lists needs a deliberate
125	  gate decision; ALWAYS is only for base machine CSRs every Andes core
126	  has (mxstatus, mclk_ctl, mdcause).
127	- **A case bound to the wrong feature** -> the gate is on for this
128	  engine but the CSR still does not exist, because the gate encodes a
129	  plausibly-related feature instead of the spec's exact existence
130	  condition.
131	
132	Cross-check against config.inc: is the gate's `_NDS_*` macro (see
133	`andes_caps_config.hpp`) on for this engine while the hart faults the
134	CSR? Then the gate is wrong.
135	
136	## Step 3: get the spec's existence condition (IM Requirement)
137	
138	The gate must encode the SPEC's existence condition, exactly -- not a
139	feature that usually comes along with it. Pull it from the AndeStar V5
140	SPA PDF (`AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf` in the andesim repo): each CSR
141	section has an `IM Requirement:` line, and "Table 13: Existence
142	configuration condition(s)" is the consolidated cross-check. See the
143	skill reference `references/spec-mining.md` for the extraction recipe
144	(PyMuPDF dump + grep), and `scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py` /
145	`tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` in the andesim repo for the
146	committed inventory.
147	
148	Two precedents, each a real bug this exact fault exposed:
149	
150	- `mcountermask_m` (0x7D1): exists when
151	  `(mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1) & (misa[20]==1)` -- BOTH perf monitor AND U-mode.
152	  It was gated PERF_MONITOR only; on the M-only premium
153	  (`NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`, perf monitor ON) the caps over-claimed
154	  it and the PB `csrr` faulted. When a condition needs both a feature
155	  and a privilege level, the privilege gate is the binding one for
156	  current engines -- it is now UMODE, matching its twins 0x7D3/0x7CE.
157	- `jvt` (0x017): Zcmt's table-jump base, NOT part of classic CoDense
158	  (`exec.it` + `uitb`). Gating it CODENSE faulted the sweep on every
159	  CoDense core. It is now ZCMT, bound to `_NDS_ZCMT_SUPPORT_INT` --
160	  a macro no current config carries, so the gate reads as off, and a
161	  future config turns it on without a code change.
162	
163	## Step 4: fix the gate, test-first (TDD)
164	
165	1. **RED**: in `vsim tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp`, model the NEW
166	   engine's config.inc shape as a helper -- copy the `premium()` pattern
167	   (line 22): `AndesCaps::none()` plus exactly the gates this engine's
168	   `_NDS_*` macros turn on. Assert the expected `supports_csr()`
169	   verdicts, including `CHECK_FALSE(c.supports_csr(0x...))` for the CSR
170	   that faulted. Build and run in the vsim container; show the failure:
171	
172	   ```sh
173	   podman run --rm -v /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim:/work -w /work \
174	     localhost/vsim-env:latest \
175	     bash -c 'cmake --build build -j && ctest --test-dir build -LE hybrid-e2e'
176	   ```
177	
178	2. **GREEN**: move/add the `case` in `andes_gate_for()`
179	   (`andes_caps.hpp`), and if the gate is new, add its `_NDS_*` binding
180	   in `andes_caps_config.hpp` (an absent macro reads as "off", never a
181	   compile error). Comment the spec condition next to the case, the way
182	   0x7D1 and 0x017 are commented today. Rebuild the sim target; rerun
183	   the unit suite green.
184	
185	The test helper IS the machine-checked record of the engine shape --
186	keep it honest against config.inc.
187	
188	## Step 5: validate with a cold-cache rerun
189	
190	The baseline capture is the caps validator: its CSR block rides the
191	batched PB sweep over the COMPLETE caps-supported list, so a clean
192	capture empirically proves every claimed CSR is `csrr`-able on this RTL.

# cmderr=3 at resume on a fresh engine: diagnosis + fix playbook

## Diagnosis (short answer)

A Program-Buffer batch faulted on the halted hart: the hart raised an
exception (cmderr=3 = "exception" in the RISC-V Debug Spec, here an
illegal instruction) while executing instructions the hybrid transport
placed in the Debug Module's Program Buffer. On a FRESHLY CONFIGURED
engine the concrete cause is almost always one of two things, and both
fire during the reset-baseline capture that runs at the very start of
resume:

1. **The batched CSR sweep hit a caps over-claimed CSR.** The caps map
   (`andes_caps.hpp` + `andes_caps_config.hpp`) claims the new engine
   implements a CSR its RTL does not have. The drain-side sweep executes
   `csrr` on it in the Program Buffer, the hart raises illegal
   instruction, and the whole batch aborts. This is the expected failure
   mode of a new engine config: the caps gates were tuned for the old
   engines and the new config.inc turns a different set of `_NDS_*`
   knobs on.

2. **mstatus.FS/VS is Off (or WARL-pinned off) for the FPR/V sweeps.**
   The capture and resume enable FS/VS before any `fld`/`fsd`/`vsetvl`/
   `vle8.v`/`vse8.v` Program-Buffer execution. If the new engine has no
   F/D or no V extension at all (while the QEMU leg drained FP/V state
   and set `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`/`HYBRID_FLAG_V`), the mstatus enable write
   pins FS/VS to 0 and the very first FP/V instruction in the Program
   Buffer raises illegal instruction -> cmderr=3.

Why "at resume" on a fresh engine specifically: the reset-baseline cache
key includes the sim binary's mtime and size
(`vsim src/hybrid/reset_baseline.hpp:26-35`), so a freshly built engine
ALWAYS misses the cache. On a miss, `apply_resume_from_qemu` captures the
baseline first (`vsim src/simulator.hpp:217-238`): it halts the freshly
reset hart and runs a FULL drain with the CSR sweep enabled
(`capture_reset_baseline`, `src/simulator.hpp:349-393`,
`drain.set_csr_sweep(true)` at line 358). That sweep rides the batched
`csrr`+`sd` Program Buffer path over the COMPLETE caps-supported CSR
list -- so one over-claimed CSR faults the batch before the restore even
starts. The exception escapes to the top-level catch in
`vsim src/main.cpp:544`, which prints the `[critical] fatal exception:`
line you saw.

The raw message string comes from `exec_progbuf` in
`vsim src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp:201-205`. Deliberate design: no
caller may silently continue on a PB fault -- the hart would be left
partially restored/drained, which is worse than aborting.

## Step 0: read the error message you actually have

The CSR sweep bisects its own faults. On a batch fault, `csr_sweep`
re-runs the batch one CSR at a time and throws a message that NAMES the
offender (`program_buffer.hpp:314-336`):

```
csr_sweep: CSR 0x7d1 raised cmderr -- the caps map over-claims a CSR
the hart does not implement (fix andes_caps)
```

So check the full log first:

- **You see the bisected `csr_sweep: CSR 0x...` message** -> caps
  over-claim confirmed, and the offending CSR is named for you. Go to
  Step 2.
- **You see only the raw `exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr=3`**
  -> the fault is in a Program-Buffer path OUTSIDE the CSR sweep's
  bisect. On a fresh engine, in order of likelihood:
  - the FPR `fsd`/`fld` block sweep or the V `vsetvl`/`vse8.v`/`vle8.v`
    sweep, with FS/VS off or the extension absent from the RTL
    (capture: `state_drain.hpp` lines 95/109/263; resume:
    `resume_driver.hpp` lines 227/244, `pb_block_sweep` /
    `pb_v_data_sweep` in `program_buffer.hpp`);
  - a per-CSR PB `csrrw` fallback for a must-restore CSR
    (`write_csr_abstract_or_pb`, `resume_driver.hpp:452-461` -- used for
    mstatus, fcsr, vstart/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr, dcsr, mcycle, minstret): if
    the abstract write faults AND the PB csrrw faults, the CSR really
    does not exist on this hart -- for the V CSRs that means the engine
    has no V while the handoff carries V state;
  - rare: the sweep's batch faulted but no single CSR reproduced it
    (the `throw;` at `program_buffer.hpp:335`).

  Either way, Step 1 tells you what the engine really implements.

## Step 1: establish ground truth (the engine's build config)

The engine's compiled-in config is the ONLY truth about what it
implements. Do not trust QEMU: its gdbstub advertises CSRs the vsim RTL
does not implement (QEMU models a fuller core).

```sh
# the BUILD directory copy, not the external/ source tree
less $VSIM_BIN_DIR/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc
$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_<engine> --describe
```

From config.inc, note the `_NDS_*` knobs relevant to the fault:
- privilege: `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS` (1 = M-only, 2 = M+U, 3 = M+S+U)
- features: DSP / CODENSE / POWERBRAKE / STACKSAFE / ECC / PMA / ILM /
  DLM / PERF_MONITOR / TRIGGER / CLIC / SMSTATEEN / CCTL / PPI / FIO ...
- extensions: does the RTL have F/D? V? (this decides the FS/VS branch)

If the fault is the FS/VS branch (raw message during an FPR/V sweep and
config.inc shows no F/D or no V): the engine cannot receive FP/V state
at all. That is not a caps bug -- pair the engine with a matching QEMU
`-cpu` (so the plugin does not set `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`/`HYBRID_FLAG_V` for
state the target cannot hold) or pick an engine that implements the
extensions the workload uses. The rest of this playbook covers the caps
over-claim, which is the common case.

## Step 2: confirm the over-claim

Three files, three roles (all in the vsim repo):

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `src/hybrid/andes_caps.hpp` | CSR address -> `AndesGate` (spec knowledge) |
| `src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp` | `AndesGate` -> `_NDS_*` macro binding |
| `build/V<engine>/obj_sc/config.inc` | what THIS engine actually has |

Look up the named CSR's `case` in `andes_gate_for()`
(`andes_caps.hpp:60-116`). Two traps to check:

- **No case at all** -> the CSR defaults to `ALWAYS` = transported
  unconditionally. Every CSR in the ABI X-macro lists needs a deliberate
  gate decision; ALWAYS is only for base machine CSRs every Andes core
  has (mxstatus, mclk_ctl, mdcause).
- **A case bound to the wrong feature** -> the gate is on for this
  engine but the CSR still does not exist, because the gate encodes a
  plausibly-related feature instead of the spec's exact existence
  condition.

Cross-check against config.inc: is the gate's `_NDS_*` macro (see
`andes_caps_config.hpp`) on for this engine while the hart faults the
CSR? Then the gate is wrong.

## Step 3: get the spec's existence condition (IM Requirement)

The gate must encode the SPEC's existence condition, exactly -- not a
feature that usually comes along with it. Pull it from the AndeStar V5
SPA PDF (`AndeStar_V5_SPA_UM164_V1.7.pdf` in the andesim repo): each CSR
section has an `IM Requirement:` line, and "Table 13: Existence
configuration condition(s)" is the consolidated cross-check. See the
skill reference `references/spec-mining.md` for the extraction recipe
(PyMuPDF dump + grep), and `scripts/extract_csr_inventory.py` /
`tests/andes_csr/csr_inventory.csv` in the andesim repo for the
committed inventory.

Two precedents, each a real bug this exact fault exposed:

- `mcountermask_m` (0x7D1): exists when
  `(mmsc_cfg.PMNDS==1) & (misa[20]==1)` -- BOTH perf monitor AND U-mode.
  It was gated PERF_MONITOR only; on the M-only premium
  (`NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`, perf monitor ON) the caps over-claimed
  it and the PB `csrr` faulted. When a condition needs both a feature
  and a privilege level, the privilege gate is the binding one for
  current engines -- it is now UMODE, matching its twins 0x7D3/0x7CE.
- `jvt` (0x017): Zcmt's table-jump base, NOT part of classic CoDense
  (`exec.it` + `uitb`). Gating it CODENSE faulted the sweep on every
  CoDense core. It is now ZCMT, bound to `_NDS_ZCMT_SUPPORT_INT` --
  a macro no current config carries, so the gate reads as off, and a
  future config turns it on without a code change.

## Step 4: fix the gate, test-first (TDD)

1. **RED**: in `vsim tests/hybrid/andes_caps.test.cpp`, model the NEW
   engine's config.inc shape as a helper -- copy the `premium()` pattern
   (line 22): `AndesCaps::none()` plus exactly the gates this engine's
   `_NDS_*` macros turn on. Assert the expected `supports_csr()`
   verdicts, including `CHECK_FALSE(c.supports_csr(0x...))` for the CSR
   that faulted. Build and run in the vsim container; show the failure:

   ```sh
   podman run --rm -v /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim:/work -w /work \
     localhost/vsim-env:latest \
     bash -c 'cmake --build build -j && ctest --test-dir build -LE hybrid-e2e'
   ```

2. **GREEN**: move/add the `case` in `andes_gate_for()`
   (`andes_caps.hpp`), and if the gate is new, add its `_NDS_*` binding
   in `andes_caps_config.hpp` (an absent macro reads as "off", never a
   compile error). Comment the spec condition next to the case, the way
   0x7D1 and 0x017 are commented today. Rebuild the sim target; rerun
   the unit suite green.

The test helper IS the machine-checked record of the engine shape --
keep it honest against config.inc.

## Step 5: validate with a cold-cache rerun

The baseline capture is the caps validator: its CSR block rides the
batched PB sweep over the COMPLETE caps-supported list, so a clean
capture empirically proves every claimed CSR is `csrr`-able on this RTL.
Force it to re-run:

```sh
rm -rf ~/.cache/andesim   # cache keys on binary mtime+size, but be explicit
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --engine vsim:<engine> \
  --verify tests/fixtures/rt_c_hello.elf
```

- Another over-claim -> another bisected `csr_sweep: CSR 0x...` abort.
  Repeat Steps 2-4 for the named CSR until the capture is clean.
- **Expect the `--verify` field count to DROP by one per de-claimed
  CSR.** That is correct, not a regression: those fields were
  zero-vs-zero false matches before (the tolerant abstract path mirrors
  a faulting read as zero, and QEMU drains zero for a CSR the program
  never wrote). Precedent: premium went 146 -> 144 when 0x7D1 and 0x017
  left the set.

Then climb the rest of the ladder:

```sh
# coverage guard (andesim repo): inventory == matrix == ABI
bash tests/andes_csr/test_csr_coverage_complete.sh

# full e2e matrix
QEMU_BIN_DIR=... VSIM_BIN_DIR=... VSIM_QEMU=... VSIM_QEMU32=... \
VSIM_PLUGIN=/home/nick/work/andesim/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so \
JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
```

## Step 6: commit and document

Tidy First: the caps fix (behavioral) and any test-helper reshaping
(structural) are separate commits, each on a green suite. Update the
vsim `ROADMAP.md` known-limits and andesim `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` section
4.4 (what `--verify` compares) if the compared set changed. If the
coverage matrix changed, regenerate `tests/andes_csr/csr_coverage.csv`
through `scripts/classify_csr_coverage.py` -- never by hand.

## What NOT to do

- **Do not disable the CSR sweep** (`set_csr_sweep(false)` /
  `set_block_store_drain(false)`) to make the run pass. The tolerant
  per-CSR abstract path MASKS over-claims: a faulting read mirrors as
  zero, QEMU drains zero, `--verify` matches zero == zero. Both
  precedent bugs were "verified" for months this way. The batched sweep
  is the only real caps validator.
- **Do not use `--no-reset-baseline` as the fix.** It skips the liveness

- **Do not wrap the fault in a try/catch or "tolerate" the cmderr.**

2	
3	Scope: a hybrid run (`./andesim run --mode hybrid`) on a freshly configured /
4	freshly built vsim engine aborts in the accurate leg with:
5	
6	```
7	[critical] fatal exception: exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr=3
8	```
9	
10	Repos referenced:
11	- driver / plugin / harness: `/home/nick/work/andesim`
12	- vsim engine + hybrid orchestration: `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim`
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 1. What the message means
17	
18	The thrower is `exec_progbuf()` in
19	`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp` (line 201-205).
20	It writes a short instruction sequence into the RISC-V Debug Module **Program
21	Buffer**, tells the halted hart to execute it, then reads back
22	`abstractcs.cmderr`. The exception escapes to the `catch` in
23	`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/main.cpp:543` which prints the
24	`[critical] fatal exception:` line and exits 1 (so the driver then reports a
25	"plan step 1: expected exit 200, got 1" style error).
26	
27	`cmderr` is the RISC-V Debug Spec abstract-command error code:
28	
29	| cmderr | meaning |
30	|--------|---------|
31	| 1 | busy |
32	| 2 | not supported |
33	| 3 | **exception - the hart took an architectural exception while executing the injected instructions** |
34	| 4 | halt/resume |
35	| 5 | bus error |
36	
37	So cmderr=3 means: one of the instructions the resume flow injected into the
38	Program Buffer **trapped inside the hart**. In this flow only two trap classes
39	occur in practice:
40	
41	1. **Illegal instruction** - the instruction touches an extension or CSR the
42	   engine's RTL does not implement (no FPU -> `fld`/`fsd` trap; no V ->
43	   `vsetvl`/`vle8.v`/`vse8.v` trap; `csrrw` to an unimplemented CSR traps), or
44	   the extension is off in `mstatus` (FS/VS = Off, which on a core *without*
45	   the extension is WARL-pinned to Off, so the enable write silently no-ops).
46	2. **Load/store access fault** - the sweep's `ld`/`sd`/`fld`/`fsd`/
47	   `vle8.v`/`vse8.v` addresses the shared-mmap scratch page at a guest
48	   physical address the engine's memory decode does not map.
49	
50	**Important discriminator built into the code:** the Andes/M-ext CSR sweep
51	(`csr_sweep()` in the same header) catches a faulting batch, bisects it one
52	CSR at a time, and rethrows a *named* error:
53	`csr_sweep: CSR 0x... raised cmderr -- the caps map over-claims a CSR ...`.
54	Therefore, if you see the **raw** `exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr=3`
55	message, the fault is **NOT** in the Andes/M-ext CSR list. It is one of the
56	fixed Program-Buffer sequences: the GPR/FPR block sweeps, the V data sweep,
57	the Tier-B `vsetvl`, or a single `csrrw` fallback.
58	
59	---
60	
61	## 2. Where it can throw, in run order
62	
63	A first hybrid run on a fresh engine executes, inside the one vsim process,
64	in this order (`Simulator::apply_resume_from_qemu`,
65	`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/simulator.hpp:208`):
66	
67	**Phase 0 - LG3 reset-baseline capture** (runs *before* resume; a freshly
68	built engine binary always misses the `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim` cache, so this
69	always runs on the first hybrid run of a new build):
70	
71	| PB sequence | instructions | traps when |
72	|---|---|---|
73	| GPR block store | `sd x1..x30, off(x31)` | scratch page not mapped/writable |
74	| FPR block store (if state FLAG_FP) | `fsd f0..f31, off(x5)` | **engine has no FPU** (FS pinned Off -> illegal insn), or scratch fault |
75	| Andes+M-ext CSR sweep | `csrr` + `sd` per CSR | caps over-claim - but this one throws the NAMED `csr_sweep: CSR 0x...` error, not the raw one |
76	| V dump sweep (if FLAG_V) | `vsetvl` then `vse8.v v0..v24` | **engine has no V** (illegal insn), or scratch fault |
77	
78	**Phase 1 - `ResumeDriver::resume()`**
79	(`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp:146`):
80	
81	| step | PB sequence | traps when |
82	|---|---|---|
83	| FPR reload (FLAG_FP) | `fld f0..f31, off(x5)` | no FPU / scratch fault |
84	| fcsr, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, mcycle, minstret | abstract write first; on abstract cmderr, PB fallback `csrrw x0, csr, x5` | the CSR does not exist on this engine (FP/V CSRs on a no-FP/no-V core) |
85	| V reload (FLAG_V) | `vsetvl` + `vle8.v v0..v24` | no V / scratch fault |
86	| Tier-B vtype+vl | `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` | no V |
87	| GPR reload | `ld x1..x31, off(x31)` | scratch fault |
88	| Andes+M-ext restore | abstract tolerant writes only | never throws (clears cmderr per CSR) |
89	
90	Note: both phases print the identical `[critical]` line, and the andesim
91	driver *hides* vsim's `[info]` log lines (commit b86d168), so from the driver
92	you cannot tell which phase died. Section 4 shows how to tell.
93	
94	---
95	
96	## 3. Root causes on a freshly configured engine, ranked
97	
98	### RC1 (by far the most common): QEMU fast leg models MORE ISA than the new engine
99	
100	The QEMU plugin (`/home/nick/work/andesim/qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`,
101	`drain_state_into`) sets `HYBRID_FLAG_FP` / `HYBRID_FLAG_V` when the QEMU
102	*CPU model* advertises the FPU / V registers - **regardless of whether the
103	workload used them**. So even a pure scalar ELF drains FP + V state. The
104	resume then executes `fld` / `vsetvl` / `vle8.v` on an engine whose RTL has no
105	FPU / no V -> illegal instruction -> cmderr=3.
106	
107	The framework's ISA-sync mechanism is: the driver probes the engine with
108	`sim_<cfg> --print-qemu-config` and passes the result to QEMU via
109	`-readconfig` (`/home/nick/work/andesim/driver/run_plan.cpp:248-255,184-187`).

# Playbook: hybrid resume dies with `exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr=3`

Scope: a hybrid run (`./andesim run --mode hybrid`) on a freshly configured /
freshly built vsim engine aborts in the accurate leg with:

```
[critical] fatal exception: exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr=3
```

Repos referenced:
- driver / plugin / harness: `/home/nick/work/andesim`
- vsim engine + hybrid orchestration: `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim`

---

## 1. What the message means

The thrower is `exec_progbuf()` in
`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp` (line 201-205).
It writes a short instruction sequence into the RISC-V Debug Module **Program
Buffer**, tells the halted hart to execute it, then reads back
`abstractcs.cmderr`. The exception escapes to the `catch` in
`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/main.cpp:543` which prints the
`[critical] fatal exception:` line and exits 1 (so the driver then reports a
"plan step 1: expected exit 200, got 1" style error).

`cmderr` is the RISC-V Debug Spec abstract-command error code:

| cmderr | meaning |
|--------|---------|
| 1 | busy |
| 2 | not supported |
| 3 | **exception - the hart took an architectural exception while executing the injected instructions** |
| 4 | halt/resume |
| 5 | bus error |

So cmderr=3 means: one of the instructions the resume flow injected into the
Program Buffer **trapped inside the hart**. In this flow only two trap classes
occur in practice:

1. **Illegal instruction** - the instruction touches an extension or CSR the
   engine's RTL does not implement (no FPU -> `fld`/`fsd` trap; no V ->
   `vsetvl`/`vle8.v`/`vse8.v` trap; `csrrw` to an unimplemented CSR traps), or
   the extension is off in `mstatus` (FS/VS = Off, which on a core *without*
   the extension is WARL-pinned to Off, so the enable write silently no-ops).
2. **Load/store access fault** - the sweep's `ld`/`sd`/`fld`/`fsd`/
   `vle8.v`/`vse8.v` addresses the shared-mmap scratch page at a guest
   physical address the engine's memory decode does not map.

**Important discriminator built into the code:** the Andes/M-ext CSR sweep
(`csr_sweep()` in the same header) catches a faulting batch, bisects it one
CSR at a time, and rethrows a *named* error:
`csr_sweep: CSR 0x... raised cmderr -- the caps map over-claims a CSR ...`.
Therefore, if you see the **raw** `exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr=3`
message, the fault is **NOT** in the Andes/M-ext CSR list. It is one of the
fixed Program-Buffer sequences: the GPR/FPR block sweeps, the V data sweep,
the Tier-B `vsetvl`, or a single `csrrw` fallback.

---

## 2. Where it can throw, in run order

A first hybrid run on a fresh engine executes, inside the one vsim process,
in this order (`Simulator::apply_resume_from_qemu`,
`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/simulator.hpp:208`):

**Phase 0 - LG3 reset-baseline capture** (runs *before* resume; a freshly
built engine binary always misses the `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim` cache, so this
always runs on the first hybrid run of a new build):

| PB sequence | instructions | traps when |
|---|---|---|
| GPR block store | `sd x1..x30, off(x31)` | scratch page not mapped/writable |
| FPR block store (if state FLAG_FP) | `fsd f0..f31, off(x5)` | **engine has no FPU** (FS pinned Off -> illegal insn), or scratch fault |
| Andes+M-ext CSR sweep | `csrr` + `sd` per CSR | caps over-claim - but this one throws the NAMED `csr_sweep: CSR 0x...` error, not the raw one |
| V dump sweep (if FLAG_V) | `vsetvl` then `vse8.v v0..v24` | **engine has no V** (illegal insn), or scratch fault |

**Phase 1 - `ResumeDriver::resume()`**
(`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp:146`):

| step | PB sequence | traps when |
|---|---|---|
| FPR reload (FLAG_FP) | `fld f0..f31, off(x5)` | no FPU / scratch fault |
| fcsr, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, mcycle, minstret | abstract write first; on abstract cmderr, PB fallback `csrrw x0, csr, x5` | the CSR does not exist on this engine (FP/V CSRs on a no-FP/no-V core) |
| V reload (FLAG_V) | `vsetvl` + `vle8.v v0..v24` | no V / scratch fault |
| Tier-B vtype+vl | `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` | no V |
| GPR reload | `ld x1..x31, off(x31)` | scratch fault |
| Andes+M-ext restore | abstract tolerant writes only | never throws (clears cmderr per CSR) |

bit1 FP, bit2 V, bit3 ANDES, bit4 M_EXT. `flags = 0x1f` on a scalar workload
with a scalar engine confirms RC1 (QEMU over-advertised). A python decoder
exists at `/home/nick/work/andesim/tools/orchestrator/abi.py`.

**Step 4 - pinpoint the throwing phase.** Run the vsim accurate-leg command
by hand (from the dry run) with two additions:

```sh
$SIM <elf> --resume-from-qemu state-0.bin ... --log-level 1
```

- No `hybrid: reset baseline ...` info line before the crash -> died in the
  LG3 **baseline-capture drain** (phase 0). (The driver hides `[info]` lines;
  running by hand shows them.)
- Add `--no-reset-baseline` to skip phase 0 entirely; if the crash persists,
  it is in `resume()` proper. Either way the root-cause set is the same
  (section 2 tables), this just tells you which sweep fired first.

**Step 5 - sanity-check the pairing itself.**
- The ELF march must fit the engine: an `-march=rv64gcv` fixture cannot run on
  a V-less engine in *any* mode. Cross-check with a standalone cycle run:
  `./andesim run --mode cycle --engine verilator:<cfg> <elf>`.
- A known-good control: the same hybrid command on `verilator:ax45mpv_premium`
  should pass end to end; that isolates the problem to the new engine's
  config/pairing, not the harness.

## 5. Fixes

**Fix 1 - regenerate the ISA sync (empty qemu.cfg).**
In `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim`:

```sh

./build_vsim.sh          # or re-run the cmake build for the engine target
$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_<cfg> --print-qemu-config   # now non-empty
```

The rebuilt binary embeds `build/V<cfg>/obj_sc/qemu.cfg`; the driver picks it
up automatically on the next `andesim run` (no driver change needed).

**Fix 2 - make the family match an instantiable QEMU model.**
The engine name's prefix before the first `_` must be a real Andes QEMU CPU
(`qemu-system-riscv64 -cpu help | grep andes`), because both the qemu.cfg
`driver=` name and (ideally) the fast leg's `-cpu` derive from it. If your
fresh engine is not in the ax45mpv family, know that today the driver still
pins `-cpu andes-ax45mpv` for the hybrid fast leg
(`driver/engine_registry.cpp:52-53`) - the qemu.cfg globals for another
family will not apply. Options, in order of preference:
- Framework fix: derive the fast-leg `-cpu` from the accurate engine's family
  (same `REGEX REPLACE "_.*$"` rule) instead of hardcoding ax45mpv - this is
  the real root-cause repair for non-ax45mpv engines.
- Interim: reproduce the shell harness pairing manually - `tests/e2e.sh`
  takes `QEMU_CPU=andes-<family>,vlen=<VLEN>` (see
  `scripts/run_e2e.sh:123-124` for the ax66_makatau <-> andes-ax66,vlen=128
  precedent) and runs the same two-leg flow.

**Fix 3 - extension ON in the base model but absent in the engine.**
The converter never emits `off`, so pick a base QEMU model whose defaults are
a subset of the engine ISA (Fix 2 usually achieves this: the same-family
model matches by construction), or extend
`config_inc_to_qemu_cfg.py::_collect_isa_props` to force-off extensions the
config lacks (`v`, `f`, `d` are the ones that bite: their state transport
executes real instructions in the Program Buffer).

**Fix 4 - memory map (RC2).**
The engine must map `[--shared-mem-base, base + mem_size + 4096)` as plain
RAM in hybrid mode. Check the fresh config's `NDS_ILM_BASE` / `NDS_DLM_BASE`
do not fall inside the window (default window: `0x0 .. 0x08001000` for the
128 MiB default), and `--print-memmap` shows the interconnect actually
decoding it. If the program needs the whole window, remember the top page is
reserved for the transport scratch - the driver already rejects ELFs that
reach into it, but a shrunken engine RAM window is the engine's problem to
fix, not the driver's.

**Fix 5 - caps map (only if the error is the NAMED csr_sweep variant, or a
poll timeout/hang).**
Bind the new config.inc macro in
`/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/andes_caps_config.hpp`
(absent macro reads as "feature off" - so a renamed macro silently drops the
gate) and/or add the CSR's gate case in `andes_gate_for()`
(`andes_caps.hpp` - an unlisted CSR defaults to ALWAYS = transported
unconditionally). Validate offline without running anything:

```sh
python3 /home/nick/work/andesim/scripts/config_inc_to_andes_caps.py \
    /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/V<cfg>/obj_sc/config.inc
# must equal the "andes_csrs" list from `sim_<cfg> --describe`
# drift guard: tests/andes_sim/test_andes_caps_parity.sh
```

**Verify the fix.**

```sh
./andesim run --mode hybrid --engine verilator:<cfg> --trigger marker --verify <elf>
JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh        # regression sweep on the stock engine
```

`--verify` matters here: it keeps the full drain and diffs the round-trip, so
an ISA fix that merely stops the crash but drops state (e.g. V silently off
on both sides now) is caught by the state diff, and a fresh reset-baseline is
captured for the new binary automatically (cache key includes the sim
binary's mtime/size, so no stale-baseline cleanup is needed).

## 6. Quick reference

Fault-to-cause map for the raw error:

| first faulting PB insn | likely cause |
|---|---|
| `fsd`/`fld` (FPR sweep) | state FLAG_FP set, engine has no FPU -> RC1 |
| `vsetvl`, `vle8.v`, `vse8.v` | state FLAG_V set, engine has no V -> RC1 |
| `csrrw x0, <csr>, x5` (fallback) | abstract write NAK'd then CSR truly absent (fcsr/vstart/... on no-FP/no-V core) -> RC1 |
| `ld`/`sd` (GPR sweep) | scratch page unmapped/blocked -> RC2 |

Key files:

| file | role |
|---|---|
| `vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/program_buffer.hpp` | thrower; `exec_progbuf`, `pb_block_sweep`, `csr_sweep`, `pb_v_data_sweep` |
| `vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` | resume order; `write_csr_abstract_or_pb` fallback |
| `vsim_andesim/src/simulator.hpp` | `apply_resume_from_qemu`: baseline capture runs before resume |
| `vsim_andesim/src/hybrid/andes_caps{,_config}.hpp` | CSR capability gates from config.inc |
| `vsim_andesim/cmake/VerilatorHelpers.cmake` | qemu.cfg generation + family-name rule |
| `andesim/driver/run_plan.cpp` | `--print-qemu-config` probe -> `-readconfig` |
